subject: general
question: One pipe can fill a tank in 3 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 12 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, then how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Filling rate = 1/3, emptying rate = 1/12

Net rate = 1/3 − 1/12 = 1/4

Time for full tank = 4 min

Half tank time = 4 ÷ 2

**∴ Answer = 2 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Filling pipe = 3 minutes

Emptying pipe = 12 minutes

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM of times

**Calculation:**

 
 

 Pipe
 Time (min)
 Total Work
 Efficiency
 
 
 
 

 Filling
 3
 12
 4
 
 

 Emptying
 12
 −1
 
 

⇒ Net efficiency = 4 − 1 = 3

⇒ Time for full tank = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 minutes

⇒ Time for half tank = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 2 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method

Take total work as LCM of given times to simplify efficiency calculation

Efficiency Concept

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

Pipes Rule

Filling adds work, emptying subtracts work
